test_title: PYST 44: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Tendulkar Committee revised India's methodology for measuring poverty. As per the Tendulkar Committee, which criterion is considered to measure poverty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumption expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tendulkar Committee**, headed by **Suresh Tendulkar**, was constituted by the Government of India in **2005** to review the methodology for estimating poverty in India.
 
• The committee recommended a shift from the earlier method of measuring poverty based on **calorie intake** to a broader metric based on **consumption expenditure.**
 
• **Consumption expenditure** includes expenses on food, health, education, and other basic needs, providing a more comprehensive measure of poverty.
 
• It also proposed using **implicit price indices** derived from the **National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO)** data to calculate poverty lines, ensuring better alignment with actual consumption patterns.
 
• The Tendulkar methodology was used to estimate poverty lines for both **urban** and **rural areas**, accounting for regional variations in consumption and living standards.
 
• As per the committee's methodology, the national poverty line was set at a monthly per capita expenditure of **₹816** for rural areas and **₹1000** for urban areas in **2004-05.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calorie Intake:**

 
 
• Earlier methods of poverty estimation, such as those by the Planning Commission, relied heavily on **calorie intake** to define poverty lines.
 
• The calorie-based poverty line focused on providing the minimum required caloric energy—**2400 kcal** for rural areas and **2100 kcal** for urban areas.
 
• However, this approach was criticized for ignoring other essential factors such as **healthcare, education, and housing.**
 
 
 
• **Income:**
 
 
• Income-based poverty measurement focuses on the **earning capacity** of individuals or households.
 
• This metric has limitations as it does not account for **inequalities in consumption** or access to services.
 
• India does not officially use income as the sole criterion for poverty estimation.
 
 
 
• **Employment Status:**
 
 
• While employment status is crucial for understanding economic stability, it is not directly used for poverty estimation in India.
 
• Unemployment or informal employment can contribute to poverty, but measures like the Tendulkar methodology rely on actual **expenditure data** rather than employment data.
 
 
 
• **Key Developments Post-Tendulkar Committee:**
 
 
• The **Rangarajan Committee**, established in **2012**, revised the Tendulkar methodology and adopted a new method for poverty calculation, focusing on **basic needs.**
 
• It updated poverty lines to ₹972 per capita per month for rural areas and ₹1407 for urban areas in **2011-12.**
 
• India's poverty estimation has evolved to include broader metrics like the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which considers factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO):**

 
 
• The NSSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, conducts household surveys that are crucial for poverty estimation.
 
• Data from NSSO surveys forms the basis of poverty lines recommended by the Tendulkar and Rangarajan Committees.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**
 
 
• The MPI, developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**, measures poverty across multiple dimensions.
 
• India's MPI score is based on factors like **health, education, and living standards** instead of income or expenditure alone.
 
 

134:T2
